title: 初二六段三题四选：折页地图里的线索
instruction: 独立选做阅读：阅读全部六段和五处词语释义，回答3题；每题从A、B、C、D中选出最合适的一项，每题2分，共6分。故事事例为虚构，请依据本文作者的观点和具体语境作答。
source_notice: 参照北师大实验标签2026初二公开原PDF第十独立选做阅读：六段好奇心随笔，第3段日常例证、五处行内词注、三题各A/B/C/D四选，各2分共6分；不是初一三选研究报告，也不含前四道语法或选做总10分。原题页、键页及完整文字已归档，题册宣称12题页而公开重排10题页的冲突保留，原校施测身份未独立认证，原键非gold。源57D的理解缺口定义更精确，但B与首段学习成长概括也有支持，原风险保留不静默改双gold；新第1题限定第二段定义，第2题问第三段例证作用，第3题检验限定情境应用。新六段故事为虚构的乐谱/折页册/读书卡学习经历，五处词注保留，非原蜡烛燃烧指引、科学实验或学生能力标定。正文、题干、候选、汉字词注与输出分别计量，不称难度或用时等值；三稿同源操作/好奇心日常交流主题家族，逐候选依据为作者自审，不作独立教研、学生、商用或生产验证。
paragraphs: Being curious does not require a collection of difficult facts. Sometimes it begins when an everyday thing refuses to fit our first explanation. We may have used a leaflet, a game or a small tool many times without thinking about one of its details. Another person’s question can make that unnoticed detail suddenly interesting, even when the object itself has not changed.

The writer’s starting point is a gap (差距) between an observation and an explanation we can give for it. We recognise that we do not yet understand something and want to explore it. A small clue (线索), such as a repeated shape, may draw our attention to that gap. Having a ready answer is not a condition for being curious. Nor must the unanswered question be important to everybody else before we may ask it.

Here is a fictional afternoon at our school’s local-history club. I was opening a visitor booklet when a friend asked me to fold back (向后折叠) its right-hand page. I thought she only wanted to save space on the table. Then I noticed that half a bridge drawn on one page joined the other half on the page below. The booklet’s small arrows suddenly made sense. I had always read its pages separately, so I had never noticed their connection. We checked the booklet’s instructions together, and they confirmed how this particular fold-out picture was meant to work.

My friend had not discovered a rule for every map or leaflet. She knew a feature of this booklet that I had overlooked. What mattered to me was the question her action raised: why did those arrows point across the fold? Once I noticed the problem, I could examine the page differently. An ordinary object had become a chance to learn because I recognised that my first explanation was incomplete.

People bring different experiences to the same material. One person notices a word; another notices a pattern or a change in a picture. We can pause (暂停) before deciding that our own first reading is enough. Asking what another person has noticed may open a useful conversation. We still need to examine the evidence, because a confident explanation can be mistaken. A disagreement can therefore be helpful when it leads both people to look more closely at the object.

We can approach (处理) a new puzzle by noticing what we cannot explain, asking someone about it and checking the available evidence. This does not promise that every puzzle will be solved straight away. A better question may be the first result. For the writer, that willingness to revise an incomplete explanation matters more than collecting answers that we never examine. Curiosity leaves room for another look, even at something we thought we already knew.

questions.stem: In Paragraph 2, which situation marks the beginning of curiosity?
options: A
You wait until everyone else considers your question important.
B
You notice something you cannot explain and want to explore it.
C
You collect a ready answer without noticing what it explains.
D
You decide that seeing an object often means fully understanding it.
questions.rationale: A：第二段明确不必先对所有人重要；B：第二段把无法解释且想探究作为起点；C：无理解缺口或追问，并非该定义起点；D：熟悉不等于理解，文章正由熟悉物产生疑问

questions.stem: What does the booklet example in Paragraph 3 mainly show?
options: A
Pictures are useful only when readers ignore the instructions.
B
All maps should be read by folding the right-hand page.
C
An everyday object can raise questions when someone reveals an overlooked detail.
D
Making booklets matters more than other history-club activities.
questions.rationale: A：两人恰恰查阅说明确认，非抛开文字；B：第四段明确不是所有地图折页的一般规则；C：朋友折页使旧有读法的缺口显现，示日常细节引问；D：未比较活动重要性，亦非制作说明

questions.stem: Which situation best represents the writer’s message?
options: A
Two pupils accept the confident speaker’s answer without opening the guide.
B
A pupil memorises sign names but ignores a sign’s unclear use.
C
Two pupils question a game-card sign and check their ideas against its guide.
D
A pupil dismisses a familiar game as having nothing new to teach.
questions.rationale: A：只凭自信不核证据，文中提醒可能错；B：仍略过功能不解之处，没有追问；C：发现疑点、交流、对照证据，符合末段方法；D：直接否定熟悉物学习机会，与文意相反
